title: Debt sustainability analysis for euro area sovereigns: a methodological framework
summary: This ECB Occasional Paper from April 2017 presents a comprehensive debt sustainability analysis (DSA) framework for euro area sovereigns, consisting of three building blocks: deterministic DSA, stochastic DSA, and other relevant indicators for liquidity and solvency risk. The framework includes benchmark and adverse shock scenarios over a ten-year horizon, probabilistic debt sustainability assessment, and a heat map methodology for summarizing risks. The paper is a methodological research document from 9 years ago.
key_points: The DSA framework comprises three main building blocks: deterministic DSA, stochastic DSA, and other relevant indicators
Deterministic DSA evaluates debt projections under benchmark and adverse narrative shock scenarios over a ten-year horizon
Stochastic DSA provides probabilistic assessment of debt sustainability including probability of debt exceeding thresholds and dispersion of simulated debt paths
Short-run liquidity risks incorporate net financing needs and a composite refinancing ease index
Medium to longer-run risks include debt maturity structure, contingent liabilities, net financial position, and governance/political risk indicators
Information from the three DSA blocks can be summarized in a heat map for overall risk assessment
why_it_matters: This 2017 ECB methodology paper provides a framework for assessing sovereign debt vulnerabilities that is still referenced in EU fiscal surveillance. While it does not address current market structure dynamics or recent macro catalysts, it represents an important methodological contribution to debt sustainability analysis that could have historical research value. The paper predates significant developments including COVID-19 fiscal responses and the 2022-2024 inflation surge.
macro_context: Debt sustainability analysis is a key component of fiscal surveillance under the Stability and Growth Pact (SGP). This framework was developed following the euro area sovereign debt crisis to improve warning systems for national fiscal policies.
